messages:
maria: Heads-up — DAST spike in staging this morning. It flagged the OAuth callback as an open redirect after the RBAC role changes from yesterday. Blocked a canary deploy. Anyone have context?

dylan: saw that alert too. looks like scanner followed 302 -> external and marked it high. the callback handler changed to return 302 for legacy clients.

sec-bot: Automated triage: severity=medium, scanner=acuity-dast, evidence_url=https://staging-logs/trace/2840056789, policy=deploy-gate. Retry count=1

priya: @maria can you paste the exact response headers from the handler? I want to check Content-Security-Policy and redirect host allowlist.

maria: pasted snippet from staging logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://oauth.example.com/callback?next=https://evil.example.net/
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ..; HttpOnly; Secure
```
Looks like legacy client param `next` isn't validated in that branch.

alex: that param was intentionally left permissive to support old SSO clients, but we have a new redirect allowlist flag in config (`ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`). Might have not been enabled in staging after the RBAC deploy.

priya: if staging config missed the allowlist, scanner will legitimately flag it. but we should decide whether this is a false positive for prod gate or a real issue we need to patch now.

maria: root cause hypothesis: RBAC role change runbook that updated service account perms also triggered the config bootstrap path which skipped loading `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` from vault due to KMS permission error. audit logs show permission denied on kms:Decrypt for secret "staging/oauth/redirects" around 03:12 UTC.

dylan: that explains it. KMS error -> fallback to permissive default -> DAST finds open redirect -> deploy gate trips. Can we confirm the KMS error in CloudAudit?

maria: pulled cloud audit: 
- principal: svc-bootstrap@redwood-staging
- method: kms.decrypt
- status: PERMISSION_DENIED
- resource: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/staging/cryptoKeys/bootstrap

priya: ok. action plan: (1) restore KMS decrypt for svc-bootstrap (short-lived grant), (2) add a pre-deploy check that validates `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` is present, (3) add a test in sdlc-e2e that simulates KMS failover so we detect permissive defaults.

maria: agree. I'll open a short-lived grant ticket and a PR to make the bootstrap fail hard if redirect allowlist is missing (fail-fast).

alex: PR idea: in bootstrap, change current behavior from `redirects = get_or_default()` to `redirects = get_or_throw()`, and record metric `bootstrap_config_missing`. Also add a one-line mitigation: temporarily block deploys with missing redirect list.

maria: created PR #4223 with the fail-fast change and a one-off deploy block check. linking: https://git.internal/redwood/platform/PR-4223

sec-bot: Noting compliance: this touched secret access flows. Marking thread for postmortem tracking tag: sdlc-config-kms-gap and paging oncall for verification.

oncall: I granted a temporary KMS decrypt role to svc-bootstrap for 2 hours (audit entry 2840056830). confirm staging now picks up allowlist.

maria: confirmed — staging now returns 200 for legacy callback (no redirect param) and DAST re-run shows no open redirect. Re-running the canary deploy.

priya: follow-ups for backlog: 1) add KMS permission smoke test in CI, 2) instrument audit-log correlation id in bootstrap so we can trace secret loads in alerts, 3) update runbook to include a step: "if deploy gate trips with DAST open redirect, check KMS decrypt failures before labeling FP."

dylan: +1. I'll add the CI smoke test. Also suggest adding an automated suppression mapping in the scanner for this specific legacy callback URL until we remove legacy clients in 2 quarters. That will stop noisy gates.

maria: assigning owners: dylan -> CI smoke test PR, priya -> runbook update + postmortem note, alex -> make metric & deploy block change more robust. I'll file the postmortem and tag engineering and security.

sec-bot: Postmortem draft created: https://incidents.redwood/postmortems/2840056789-dast-kms-bootstrap-misconfig. Labels: sdlc, kms, rbacs, dast, false-positive-mitigation

maria: thanks all. one action item before we close: ensure audit logs include the value of `principal_email` and `request_id` in the DAST alert so triage avoids digging through CloudAudit manually. small change — I'll add to the scanner alert enrichment.

priya: good call. closing thread once postmortem is up-to-date. :white_check_mark:
